card.name: News-lead words about reports and announcements
card.fires_on: Words in the first sentences of English news stories, such as a verb, time word or noun that comes just before the story says who announced or reported something. Typical cases are 'report', 'rules', 'approved', 'banned' and 'last' in 'last week'.

modes.label: Report or rules as source
modes.description: The noun naming the document or body that is the source of the news, right before details or a named group.
modes.example: according to the<< rules>>. They also stipulate tougher tsunami defenses

modes.label: Action verb or time word in a lead
modes.description: A verb of official action or a time word inside the opening sentence of a news item.
modes.example: Japan’s Nuclear Regulation Authority<< approved>> safety standards for atomic power plants that may

modes.label: Attribution after a clause
modes.description: A comma or 'the' just before a named organisation that urged or said something.
modes.example: outside the region,<< the>> National Wildlife Federation urged Tuesday. The Great

card.writes: It leans toward policy and politics terms and toward Chinese words for raising or lowering, so it adds a sense of official or policy news.
card.plain: It fires in the opening lines of news stories, at the point where an official body, report or rule is about to be named.
